source: The AB (anterior burster) neuron is electrically coupled to the PD neurons and together they form a pacemaker kernel.

source: The interactions in the network are mediated by seven chemical synapses of two types: glutamatergic and cholinergic Prinz et al., 2004.

source: We produced one hundred models of the pyloric network that displayed similar activities with values of maximal conductances distributed over wide ranges.

claim: The models become less robust as the extent of the changes increases.

claim: These studies have led to an underestimate of the role of intrinsic membrane currents in network dynamics in larger networks.

claim: This process was repeated to produce 100 different models with values of conductances distributed over large ranges.
source: We repeated this process to produce 100 different models with values of conductances distributed over large ranges.
evidence: This is stated as the procedure for generating the model database.

claim: The models were simulated for 10 s, and the final 5 s of the simulation were utilized.
source: The models were simulated for 10 s, and the final 5 s of the simulation were utilized.
evidence: This is stated as the simulation protocol for feature extraction.

claim: Spike times were calculated by finding the local maxima of the time series of the membrane potential of each cell.
source: We calculated spike times by finding the local maxima of the time series of the membrane potential of each cell.
evidence: This is stated as the method for spike detection.

claim: In the case of a regularly bursting cell, the ISI distribution is bimodal, with one peak corresponding to the intraburst ISI, and the other peak corresponding to the IBIs.
source: In the case of a regularly bursting cell, the ISI distribution is bimodal, with one peak corresponding to the intraburst ISI, and the other peak corresponding to the IBIs.
evidence: This is stated as a property of regularly bursting cells.

claim: The ISI threshold was calculated by first detecting the peaks in the histograms of ISIs and then choosing the value halfway between these peaks.
source: We calculated the ISI threshold by first detecting the peaks in the histograms of ISIs and then chose the value halfway between these peaks.
evidence: This is stated as the method for determining the ISI threshold.

claim: Using this method led to errors in burst identification in some cases, and this is a source of error and a limitation of the study.
source: Using this method led to errors in burst identification in some cases, and this is a source of error and a limitation of the study.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the burst detection method.

claim: The features extracted from each model include the mean and standard deviations of the distributions of duty cycles that each cell produces over the period of 5 s.
source: The features extracted from each model include the mean and standard deviations of the distributions of duty cycles that each cell produces over the period of 5 s.
evidence: This is stated as the features extracted for classification.

claim: The means of the distributions of the phases of the rhythm at which each cell begins and ends a burst were also calculated.
source: We also calculated the means of the distributions of the phases of the rhythm at which each cell begins and ends a burst.
evidence: This is stated as additional features extracted for classification.

claim: The activity of each trace was evaluated by first building a vector containing features of its activity.
source: The activity of each trace was evaluated by first building a vector containing features of its activity.
evidence: This is stated as the method for classification.

claim: A random forest classifier was chosen to avoid the possibility that gradient boosting machines might over fit to the training data.
source: We attempted classification of the vectors using a number of algorithms including random forest classifiers and gradient boosting machines Ho, 1995; Friedman, 2001, and we chose to use random forest classifiers to avoid the possibility that gradient boosting machines might over fit to the training data for our purposes Natekin and Knoll, 2013.
evidence: This is stated as the rationale for choosing the classifier with supporting citations.

claim: The classifier consisted of 500 decision trees (max depth = 4), where each tree was fed a different subset of the features for classification.
source: The classifier we created consisted of 500 decision trees (max depth = 4), where each tree was fed a different subset of the features for classification.
evidence: This is stated as the configuration of the classifier.

claim: A winner-takes-all vote between the trees chooses the output label of the classifier.
source: A winner-takes-all vote between the trees chooses the output label of the classifier.
evidence: This is stated as the decision mechanism of the classifier.

claim: The classifier was trained with a set of data that was manually labeled, with the help of experimentalists that study the pyloric network in the crustacean STG.
source: The classifier must first be trained with a set of data that was manually labeled, with the help of experimentalists that study the pyloric network in the crustacean STG.
evidence: This is stated as the training procedure for the classifier.

claim: When the cells were bursting in a triphasic pattern in the order PD-LP-PY, with at least two spikes per burst, the activity was considered to be pyloric.
source: When the cells were bursting in a triphasic pattern in the order PD-LP-PY, with at least two spikes per burst, we considered the activity to be pyloric (see Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as the criterion for pyloric activity with reference to Figure 1.

claim: The classifier was trained on a database of 1200 model solutions or traces featuring a wide variety of wave-forms.
source: We trained the classifier on a database of 1200 model solutions or traces featuring a wide variety of wave-forms.
evidence: This is stated as the training dataset for the classifier.

claim: Any other type of activity was considered 'not pyloric'.
source: Any other type of activity was considered 'not pyloric'.
evidence: This is stated as the classification criterion.

claim: In some cases, rhythms that displayed pyloric characteristics but also exhibited irregular features were excluded.
source: In some cases we excluded rhythms that displayed pyloric characteristics but also exhibited irregular features, such as abnormally large duty cycles, cells with low amplitude spikes, and inconsistent firing and/or bursting patterns.
evidence: This is stated as an exclusion criterion for training data.

claim: The trained classifier generalized with ≥ 95% accuracy for many, but not all models.
source: We found that the trained classifier generalized with ≥ 95% accuracy for many, but not all models.
evidence: This is stated as the performance of the classifier.

claim: To verify that the classifier properly classified the models, thousands of traces were manually checked.
source: To verify that the classifier properly classified the models we chose, we manually checked thousands of traces.
evidence: This is stated as the validation procedure for the classifier.

claim: Only models that were classified with ≥ 95% accuracy after perturbation were used in this study.
source: Only models that were classified with this level of accuracy after perturbation were used in this study.
evidence: This is stated as a selection criterion for models.

claim: On rare occasions, the classifier misclassified models that are clearly pyloric as not pyloric even though the list of features fed to the classifier were calculated properly.
source: On rare occasions, the classifier misclassified models that are clearly pyloric as not pyloric even though the list of features fed to the classifier were calculated properly.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the classifier.

claim: The percentage of misclassifications was approximately 2 – 3%, which is consistent with the accuracy of the classifier.
source: The percentage of misclassifications was approximately 2 – 3%, which is consistent with the accuracy of the classifier.
evidence: This is stated as a quantification of the classifier error rate.

claim: To analyze the sensitivity curves quantitatively, they were fit with sigmoid functions by optimizing for the sigmoidal midpoint and width parameters using a brute force approach.
source: To analyze the sensitivity curves quantitatively, we fit them with sigmoid functions. We optimized for the sigmoidal midpoint and width parameters by minimizing an error function using a brute force approach.
evidence: This is stated as the method for quantitative analysis of sensitivity curves.

claim: The output of the classifier was evaluated over two-dimensional ranges in conductance space to visualize regions where the activity is a normal pyloric rhythm.
source: We evaluated the output of the classifier over two-dimensional ranges in conductance space.
evidence: This is stated as the method for visualizing conductance space.

claim: For the synaptic conductances, three pairs were visualized: the cholinergic inputs to LP and PY from PD, the glutamatergic inputs to LP from PD and PY, and the glutamatergic inputs from PD to LP and LP to PD.
source: For the synaptic conductances, we visualized three pairs: the cholinergic inputs to LP and PY from PD, the glutamatergic inputs to LP from PD and PY, and the glutamatergic inputs from PD to LP and LP to PD.
